questions.q: Which layout is the most survivable when one motor fails?
questions.explain: The coaxial partner and the opposite pair compensate for both thrust and moment.

questions.q: What happens to a hexa when a motor fails without thrust margin?
questions.explain: Five motors pull, but the CW/CCW balance is broken; with T/W < 2 it falls.

questions.q: Why aren't fuses put on the motors?
options: They interfere with ESC telemetry and DShot
Pulsed current: it will blow for nothing
questions.explain: Fuses go on the battery, the BEC and the payload branches.

questions.q: How is the FC's BEC made redundant?
options: A big capacitor on the bus
questions.explain: If one fails, power keeps coming from the second.

questions.q: X8 arm current relative to motor current:
questions.explain: There are two motors on an arm.

questions.q: How do you simulate a motor failure in ArduPilot SITL?
questions.explain: SITL applies a multiplier to the output of the selected motors.

questions.q: What do you see in the ArduPilot log when a motor fails?
options: Battery voltage rises and current falls
questions.explain: One RCOU channel at maximum, its neighbor at minimum, RPM 0 in the ESC telemetry: the mixer compensates.

questions.q: A flat octo compared with a hexa:
options: Needs less total thrust to hover the same mass
Bigger margin, can survive two failures in favorable positions
questions.explain: Eight motors give a bigger margin and, with a favorable arrangement, survive two failures.
